'''Merrill Brian Maple''' (born November 20, 1939) is an American [[physicist]]. He is a distinguished professor of physics and holds the [[Bernd T. Matthias]] Chair in the physics department at the [[University of California, San Diego]], and conducts research at the university's Center for Advanced Nanoscience. He has also served as the director of UCSD's Institute for Pure and Applied Physical Sciences (1995-2009) and its Center for Interface and Materials Science (1990-2010).<ref name="CAN">{{cite web|url=http://can.ucsd.edu/people.php?selection=maple|title=M. Brian Maple|work=Center for Advanced Nanoscience|publisher=University of California, San Diego|accessdate=August 19, 2013}}</ref> His primary research interest is [[condensed matter physics]], involving phenomena like magnetism and superconductivity.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://www-physics.ucsd.edu/fac_staff/fac_profile/faculty_description.php?person_id=740|title=Faculty page|publisher=University of California, San Diego|accessdate=August 19, 2013}}</ref> He has authored or co-authored more than 900 scientific publications and five patents in correlated electron physics, high pressure physics, nano physics, and surface science.

==Education and career==
Maple was born November 20, 1939, in [[Chula Vista, California]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=xbeaAAAAIAAJ&q=%22maple,+merrill+brian%22 Reports of the President and the Treasurer] John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation</ref> He received BA and BS degrees in 1963 from San Diego State College (now [[San Diego State University]]). He received an MS in 1965 and a PhD in physics from UCSD in 1969, working under [[Bernd T. Matthias]] and has been on the UCSD faculty since 1973. He became an associate professor in 1977, was named a full professor in 1981 and a distinguished professor in 2005. He has held the Bernd T. Matthias endowed chair since 1990.<ref name="ACAP">{{cite web|url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?maplemb|title=M. Brian Maple|work=Array of Contemporary American Physicists|publisher=American Institute of Physics|accessdate=August 19, 2013}}</ref> From 2004 through 2010 he also served as chair of the physics department.

He has been granted a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (1984) and a [[Humboldt Research Award]] (1998). In addition to his work at UCSD he was a Bernd T. Matthias Scholar in the Center for Materials Science at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] (1993). He was granted an honorary professorship at the Trzebiatowski Institute for Low Temperature and Structure Research of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (2006) and a Science Lectureship Award at [[Chiba University]] in Tokyo (2010).

He organized and presided over a famous "Special Session on Recent Developments in High T<sub>c</sub> Superconductivity", nicknamed "the [[Woodstock of physics]]",<ref name="Chang">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/03/06/science/06supe.html?_r=0|title=Physicists Remember When Superconductors Were Hot|last=Chang|first=Kenneth|date=March 6, 2007|work=New York Times|accessdate=August 19, 2013}}</ref> during the March 1987 meeting of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1987-04-05-me-416-story.html|title=Resistance Movement : Breakthroughs in Electrical Superconductors Have Scientists Charged Up|last=Scott|first=Janny|date=April 5, 1987|work=Los Angeles Times|access-date=August 19, 2013}}</ref> The session, which was added to the agenda at the last minute, dealt with newly discovered high temperature superconductors. It featured 51 speakers, limited to 5–10 minutes per speaker, and lasted until 3:15&nbsp;am. More than 1,800 scientists crammed into the lecture room and another 2,000 watched on television.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.aip.org/png/images/woodstockrelease.pdf|title=Highlights from the papers presented at the American Physical Society meeting in New York City, March 16–20, 1987|publisher=American Institute of Physics|accessdate=August 19, 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013222436/http://www.aip.org/png/images/woodstockrelease.pdf|archivedate=October 13, 2008|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Maple also presided over a 20th-anniversary recognition and review of the famous session, held at the American Physical Society's 2007 meeting in Denver.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://docs.google.com/a/alumni.stanford.edu/viewer?a=v&pid=gmail&attid=0.1.1&thid=140bb6fe55cc9de2&mt=application/pdf&url=https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/?ui%3D2%26ik%3De67a70bc03%26view%3Datt%26th%3D140bb6fe55cc9de2%26attid%3D0.1.1%26disp%3Dsafe%26zw&sig=AHIEtbQ1oN0GjeccW_E7UR0kR4NZUHC2EA|title=20th Anniversary of High Tc Superconductivity 'Woodstock' Session|work=Forum on the History of Physics|publisher=American Physical Society|accessdate=26 August 2013}}</ref>

==Recognition==
* In 1987 he was named Distinguished Alumnus of the Year by UCSD.<ref name = "bio" />
* In 1988 he was named Distinguished Alumnus of the Year by SDSU College of Sciences.
* In 1996 he received the [[David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics]] from the American Physical Society.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/awards/adler.cfm|title=David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics|publisher=American Physical Society|accessdate=August 23, 2013}}</ref>
* In 2000 he received the [[James C. McGroddy Prize for New Materials]] from the American Physical Society for "the synthesis of novel d and f electron materials and for the study of their physics."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/units/dmp/awards/recipient.cfm?first_nm=M.&last_nm=Maple&year=2000|title=2000 James C. McGroddy Prize for New Materials Recipient|work=Division of Material Physics|publisher=American Physical Society|accessdate=August 19, 2013}}</ref>
* In 2004 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://biology.ucsd.edu/news/article_042004.html|title=Two UCSD Professors In Biology And Physics Elected To National Academy Of Sciences|last=McDonald|first=Kim|date=April 20, 2004|publisher=UCSD|accessdate=August 19, 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130822192118/http://biology.ucsd.edu/news/article_042004.html|archive-date=August 22, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Other awards include the [[Bernd T. Matthias Prize]] for Superconducting Materials, the [[Frank Spedding|Frank H. Spedding Award]] for Research on Rare Earths,<ref name = "CAN" /> and the [[David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics|David Adler Lectureship Award]] (1996).
* He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name = "CAN" />
